items.headline: Brazil moves to become one of the first countries in the Americas to eliminate mother-to-child hepatitis B transmission
items.summary: Brazil has formally submitted its dossier to the World Health Organization and the Pan American Health Organization requesting validation that it has eliminated mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B as a public health problem. The submission was presented at a ceremony attended by Brazil's president, health minister, and the WHO director-general, marking a major step toward wiping out a preventable infection that can cause chronic liver disease in children.
items.why_it_matters: If validated, it would make Brazil one of the first countries in the Americas to officially end a leading cause of childhood chronic liver disease, protecting future generations from lifelong infection.
